faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Questions about the Berlin water map — fountains, Refill, public taps, and how to use the map.
faq.projectFaqsTitle: Questions about our initiative and goals
faq.mapFaqsTitle: Questions about using our water map

questions.question: Why can’t I find most fountains on Google Maps?
questions.answer:
[The Berliner Wasserbetriebe (BWB)](https://www.bwb.de/de/trinkbrunnen.php), the company that installs the fountains, only lists them on their own website. They do not integrate the locations with Google Maps. Instead, they provide a downloadable .kml file with all fountain coordinates.

We’ve made it easier for you by turning that data into a Google Maps layer you can add directly to your phone. We also included other public water sources such as libraries, open public schools, Refill spots, and dm stores with water dispensers or customer restrooms.

For even more refill points, check out [Refill](https://refill-deutschland.de/) Berlin, which lists businesses and organizations participating in their program.

questions.question: How does water map work?
questions.answer: We’ve taken the BWB data and other sources and created a map you can add to your Google Maps app as an extra layer. This way, you can see all known public water points right in your regular map view.

questions.question: How do I add this map to my Google Maps app?
questions.answer: Visit our [Berlin water fountain map](/{lang}/map) page, tap the download button, and the new layer will be added to your Google Maps app. You can remove it anytime.

questions.question: Can I suggest a new location for the map?
questions.answer: Yes! Just write to us at the address listed in the footer.

questions.question: What areas are you focusing on first?
questions.answer: We are starting with underserved districts outside the busy city center, beginning in Pankow and Lichtenberg.

questions.question: Who decides where new drinking fountains are installed?
questions.answer: The Berlin Senate (Senatsverwaltung) decides that together with the Berliner Wasserbetriebe and local district authorities.

questions.question: Who funds the installation and maintenance of fountains?
questions.answer: The Berlin Senate funds both the installation and maintenance, and the Berliner Wasserbetriebe manages the work.

questions.question: How much does it cost to install and maintain a fountain?
questions.answer: Installing one fountain costs around €12,000–15,000. Maintenance, including water testing, costs about €3,700 per year.

questions.question: Are the fountains safe to drink from?
questions.answer: Yes. Water from each fountain is tested every 4 weeks to ensure it meets safety standards.

questions.question: Why do fountains run water constantly? Isn’t that wasteful?
questions.answer: The constant flow prevents water from standing in the pipes, which reduces the risk of bacterial growth. The drained water is used to water trees in some locations.

questions.question: When are the fountains operational during the year?
questions.answer: They operate from May to October each year to avoid freezing in winter.

questions.question: What data does the drinking fountain database include?
questions.answer: We analyzed BVV archives to identify documented inquiries (Anfragen) related to drinking fountains. In addition, we requested documents through local district representatives. Based on the materials we found, we compiled a database of fountain locations and attached links to the original official documents for each entry. The database will be continuously expanded as new parliamentary inquiries and additional data become available.

questions.question: How can I hide or show water sources in Google Maps?
questions.answer:
If you don’t want to see water sources from the custom map in the Google Maps app, tap “You” at the bottom of the screen, scroll all the way down, and select “Maps.” Then tap the name of the map and choose “Close” to hide the water sources. This will temporarily remove the map from your view.

You can learn more on the [official Google support page](https://support.google.com/maps/answer/3045850?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DiOS).

questions.question: Where did you get the data for the map?
questions.answer: The complete list of drinking fountains comes from [Berliner Wasserbetriebe (BWB)](https://www.bwb.de/de/trinkbrunnen.php), other refill spots from [Refill Germany](https://refill-deutschland.de/), the list of Volkshochschulen (VHS) from the [official City of Berlin website](https://www.berlin.de/vhs/volkshochschulen/), the list of libraries from the [Verbund der Öffentlichen Bibliotheken Berlins website](https://www.voebb.de/aDISWeb/app?service=direct/0/Home/$DirectLink&sp=SPROD00&sp=SWI01000154&noRedir), and dm stores with a water dispenser (Wasserspender) or customer restroom (Kunden-WC) based on information published on the [dm website](https://www.dm.de/).

questions.question: How can I help support your initiative?
questions.answer: Spread the word about our [Berlin water fountain map](/{lang}/map) — let your friends know about it or share it through your channels. Feel free to contact us to get stickers and flyers if you’d like to get more involved. We are happy to hear about other projects to collaborate with or get in touch with local authorities.

questions.question: Are there fountains in Berlin to drink water?
questions.answer: Yes. Berlin has 238 public drinking fountains operated by [Berliner Wasserbetriebe (BWB)](https://www.bwb.de/de/trinkbrunnen.php), plus hundreds of Refill spots, public buildings, and other free water points. Our [water fountains in Berlin map](/{lang}/map) shows nearly 1,000 locations across the city. Fountains typically run from May to October each year.

questions.question: How can I find free drinking water near me in Berlin?
questions.answer: Open our [water fountains in Berlin map](/{lang}/map) on your phone and add it as a layer in Google Maps. You can then see public drinking fountains, Refill spots, and other free water points near your current location across Berlin.

mentions.title: In the media
mentions.subtitle: Media outlets and communities covering our project

news.title: Project Start
news.content: The initiative was officially kickstarted as the part of the citizen activation program of the Club Dialog e.V.

news.title: Engagement with Berliner Wasserbetriebe
news.content: Our suggestion for a fountain location in Pankow has been accepted for consideration and is now on the list for future possible locations. BWB drinking fountations map integration.

news.title: Engagement with Refill
news.content: Exchanged experience and insights about the water sources mapping. Refill spots map integration.

news.title: Engagement with the Pankow District Council
news.content: The Left Faction agreed to submit a citizen petition to the Pankow District Council for future discussion.

news.title: Water Map Beta Launch
news.content: We released a beta version of our map showing all known public water points in Berlin, and shared it for feedback with other organizations.

news.title: Website Launch
news.content: We launched a website where you can find information about our project and share your thoughts.

news.title: Info Campaign Launch
news.content: We're excited to announce the launch of our info campaign! Our goal is to share more about our initiative with the public across different districts. To support this, we've also created a new map in English—especially for this campaign.

news.title: 4,500 Berliners use our map
news.content: An important milestone: Over 4,500 people in Berlin have already opened our map to find free drinking water points.

news.title: Multilingual Map - NEW: Now also in Russian
news.content: Our map is now available in Russian! This helps more Berliners find drinking fountains and refill points and save the map to Google Maps.

news.title: Information on planned drinking fountains in Pankow
news.content: Thanks to a small inquiry to the BVV Pankow and with the help of the Linksfraktion in the BVV Pankow, we received official information about planned drinking fountains in the district.

news.title: Exchange with the Senate Administration (SenMVKU)
news.content: The Senate confirmed: There is no budget in 2025 for new drinking fountains.

news.title: Contact with Lichtenberg civic engagement office
news.content: We are talking with the Lichtenberg civic engagement office to explore what funding or participation opportunities exist at the district level for drinking fountain installations.

news.title: New inquiries to district authorities in other districts
news.content: We are collecting information on planned drinking fountains and submitted new small inquiries to various districts to get a more complete picture for Berlin.

news.title: 10,000+ Map Views
news.content: We're excited to share that our water maps were viewed over 10,000 times! We'll continue working on water fountain installation this year and keep you updated.

news.title: Thank You to Carla Assmann for the Parliamentary Inquiry
news.content: Thank you to [Carla Assmann](https://www.linksfraktion-neukoelln.de/ueber-uns/bezirksverordnete/carla-assmann/) (Die Linke Neukölln) for submitting a small parliamentary inquiry on our behalf. The data we received regarding planned fountain locations will be available on our website shortly.

news.title: Thank You to Dennis Egginger-Gonzalez for the Parliamentary Inquiry
news.content: We would like to sincerely thank [Dennis Egginger-Gonzalez](https://linksfraktion-sz.de/verordnete/dennis-egginger-gonzalez/) (Die Linke Steglitz) for submitting a small parliamentary inquiry ([Kleine Anfrage](https://bvv-steglitz-zehlendorf.berlin.de/pi-r/ka020_r.asp?KALFDNR=2074)) on our behalf. The data we received regarding planned fountain locations will be available on our website shortly.

news.title: District Data for Fountain Installation Requests is Online
news.content: The list of locations with requests for fountain installations is now online. Data for the districts of Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf, Pankow, and Steglitz-Zehlendorf is now [available on our website](https://www.water4all.com.de/{lang}/fountains/locations).

news.title: All BVV fountain requests are now online
news.content: We have added all the details for fountain locations requested through Berlin’s district councils (BVV). You can now find the full list of proposed sites for every district on our website.

news.title: New Guide: How to request a drinking fountain
news.content: Our new [guide on our website](https://www.water4all.com.de/{lang}/fountains/guide) for requesting drinking fountains is now live. We have put together a step-by-step walkthrough on how to propose a fountain installation in your local area.

news.title: 60,000 Map Views
news.content: Our maps have been viewed 60,000 times as of July 1, 2026. We are happy to help you find free drinking water sources across Berlin.

news.title: Discussions with Local Politicians During Election Season
news.content: We are taking advantage of the election season to continue our discussions with local politicians about the importance of access to drinking water.

news.title: dm Stores with Water Dispensers and Restrooms
news.content: Based on user feedback, we have added a list of dm stores that offer water dispensers and/or customer restrooms.

news.title: 100,000+ Map Views
news.content: Our maps have been viewed more than 100,000 times as of August 2026. Thank you for using them to find free drinking water across Berlin — we will keep improving the map.

news.title: Featured by the Federal Association of Russian-Speaking Parents
news.content: The [Bundesverband russischsprachiger Eltern e.V. (BVRE)](https://www.instagram.com/bvre_e.v/p/DcRAnBPMt2U/) presented our initiative as part of the “Kommunal Aktiv” project — highlighting the water map, the open fountain database, and the guide for citizen requests.

mentionSummaries.1: Featured our project in a deep dive into how to make Berlin's urban environment more accessible and comfortable.
mentionSummaries.2: Shared our mission with the local eco-community, highlighting why public fountains are key to a more sustainable city.
mentionSummaries.3: Highlighted our work while discussing water accessibility, showing residents how to easily find free water sources across Berlin.
mentionSummaries.4: Video interview and walk-and-talk with our co-founder Masha, showcasing different water sources in Berlin.
